children: Energy stocks grabbed the spotlight this week as Wall Street digested a wave of third-quarter earnings, led by major reports from oil giants Exxon Mobil
, Chevron
, and refiner Phillips 66

While uncertainty around energy prices can influence earnings expectations across the sector, companies trading at discounts to their fundamentals may offer opportunities for investors looking for growth at a reasonable price.
In this week's earnings recap, seven tickers reported results, out of which six companies exceeded EPS expectations, while one missed expectations. Except for EQT Corp
, all companies topped revenue expectations.
Below are the latest quarterly reports from some of the key players who reported results this week:
ExxonMobil
rose Friday after posting
that beat Wall Street expectations, capitalizing on the strength of surging gasoline and diesel prices that lifted its refining results to an all-time high. ExxonMobil

plans to spend more than $100B through 2030 to boost global energy supplies, including ~10% focused on its refining business, particularly at its existing facilities, including the Baton Rouge, Louisiana, and Beaumont, Texas, refineries, to improve production yields and raise refined product margins.
Shares in Chevron
also advanced after reporting
and revenues that topped Wall Street expectations, boosted by higher margins on refined product sales and higher crude oil realizations.
Phillips 66
closed up 1.9% in Wednesday's trading after reporting its

that also beat Wall Street estimates, powered by strength in its refining business as the conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine have disrupted global supplies of diesel and other fuels, pushing prices higher.
Baker Hughes
fell 5.4% in Wednesday's trading despite reporting better than expected Q3 adjusted earnings and revenues, as the Middle East conflict dented demand for oilfield services and equipment in the region.
